summary: Postgres pool and SQL execution contracts attached to implemented messenger, mail, social, and community app write plans.
claim_boundary: Execution contract only. This slice defines bounded pool configuration, ordered SQL execution plans, and a recording executor contract that preserves tenant RLS setup ordering. It does not open sqlx pools, connect to Postgres, run live transactions, perform backup/restore drills, or exercise Citus rebalancing.

facets.F1_simplicity: Pool and execution planning live in the existing shared Postgres command kernel; app crates attach a derived SQL execution plan without adding runtime dependencies.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: Every implemented write plan now carries bounded pool settings, tenant-scope-first command ordering, and application names for later live sqlx wiring. Live runtime evidence remains pending.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests reject invalid pool settings and verify the recording executor preserves tenant scope before mutations.
facets.F5_quality: Focused shared/app tests plus broad 32-package cargo check/test/clippy/fmt, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are used for this slice.
facets.F7_security_privacy: Execution plans preserve tenant scope setup before RLS-protected statements and keep parameterized SQL values out of SQL text.
facets.F11_observability: Pool application names are deterministic per microservice for future database telemetry. No runtime OpenTelemetry or database metric emission is claimed.

verification.evidence: 17 focused unit tests passed across shared Postgres command kernel and app packages.
